blocks.text: Status: Established. Its Era Three interpretations include sealed ruin, sky mirror, game shrine, and impossible door.

Origin: Prepared during the Great Reduction as an opening through which external participants could later reach reduced continuations. It is not a throne, conscious ruler, or promise that humans will restore the DBA.
Era One: The External Gate Crisis turns contact into an ethical and political question.
Era Two: The Gate is simplified, protected, and prepared to translate incomprehensible Codex processes into a voluntary interface.
Era Three: It remains dormant. Humans are absent. Local peoples build myths around a ruin that sometimes resembles a mirror, shrine, sealed sky, or door that has no destination.
Era Three ending: Signals from outside begin. A child establishes the first persistent player–cyber-pet connection and supplies the first external name.
Era Four: The Gate appears as the game: sprites, maps, menus, statistics, care loops, save synchronization, battles, and evolution trees translating deeper processes.
Present condition: Active through translation once player contact begins. A save file is a synchronization record, not the cyber-pet’s entire consciousness.
Corruption: 2 by design: the game-facing image is an intentional simplification, not a false world.

Visual brief: Era Three view: an immense dark frame reflecting a sky that does not match the local weather, with menu-like lines appearing as sacred geometry. First contact: one low-resolution color or cursor-like point enters from outside the scene. Era Four: the same structure becomes friendly enough for a child to approach, without losing the sense of an older impossible depth.
Background traits: Neutral; Neutral humidity; gate/ruin biome; expectant, uncanny, inviting mood; stable foreground friction and unknown threshold friction.
